workshops.name: ICE
workshops.title: Interactions, Control and Events
workshops.dateDetail: 13 July is the announced ECC 2027 workshop day. This birthday workshop is proposed and its acceptance is pending.
workshops.venueDetail: The announced conference campus. The birthday workshop room will be announced following confirmation.
workshops.description: This one-day workshop brings together Rodolphe’s former doctoral students and postdoctoral researchers to discuss new directions in systems and control, and to celebrate his 60th birthday. The programme follows the successive generations of his research community.
workshops.themeText: Control as interaction is the starting point. The day follows questions from geometric optimisation and collective dynamics to differential methods, biological rhythms and event-based control. Alumni are invited, in this proposed format, to connect an idea developed with Rodolphe to a question they pursue today.
workshops.registration: Registration information will be added after workshop acceptance and publication of the conference registration arrangements.
workshops.travel: The planned setting is the ECC 2027 conference campus in Brussels. Venue access and local travel details will be added once the workshop room is confirmed.

workshops.shortDescription: An alumni gathering: where shared questions began, how they evolved, and what comes next.
workshops.speakerDescription: The researchers who worked with Rodolphe as doctoral students and postdocs, and the directions their work has taken since.
workshops.programmeDescription: Nineteen alumni contributions, in order of joining Rodolphe, followed by his response and close. Four sessions of five contributions run from 09:00 to 17:20. Each slot includes a 15-minute talk and 5 minutes for questions, with two 20-minute coffee breaks and a one-hour lunch.

workshops.dateDetail: The one-day workshop date is to be confirmed. The local organiser announces the overall CDC event for 13–17 December 2027.

workshops.description: A one-day workshop celebrating Rodolphe’s 60th birthday through the collaborations and scientific conversations that connect nonlinear control, geometry, collective dynamics and biological regulation.
workshops.themeText: Feedback connects fields that often use different languages. The proposed day pairs nonlinear regulation with geometry and learning, collective behaviour with embodied rhythms, and physical systems with cellular dynamics. Conversation between these perspectives is the central aim.

workshops.shortDescription: An exchange across disciplines: the collaborations and conversations that give feedback new forms.
workshops.speakerDescription: Collaborators and fellow researchers whose work meets Rodolphe’s across geometry, nonlinear control, collective dynamics and biological regulation.
workshops.programmeDescription: Thirteen collaborator contributions and Rodolphe’s closing response, from 09:00 to 17:40. Each 30-minute slot includes a 25-minute talk and 5 minutes for questions. Four sessions of three or four contributions are separated by two 20-minute coffee breaks and a one-hour lunch. The running order is provisional.

chronologyNote: Order the 19 alumni by earliest documented year of joining Sepulchre as PhD student or postdoc. For same-year cohorts, use alphabetical surname order because exact order of arrival is not established consistently. More explicit personal career records are used for Franci and Miranda-Villatoro where they conflict with the roster. Rodolphe Sepulchre is placed last for his response and close.

chronologyCaveats.text: Date discrepancy: Sepulchre's roster says 2011–2015; Franci's personal biography states a 2012 PhD and postdoctoral research during 2012–2015 at Liège, INRIA Lille and Cambridge. Use 2012 as the more explicit personal career record; exact beginning with Sepulchre remains source-disputed.

Date discrepancy: Sepulchre's roster says 2017–2020, but Miranda-Villatoro's own Inria biography explicitly states Cambridge Research Associate March 2018–September 2020 and PhD 2018. Use the more precise 2018 personal record; 2017 is not a settled start date.
